formality: Formal address only (vykání — 2nd person plural 'Vy/jste/máte', the Czech equivalent of French 'vous' or German 'Sie'). Never use informal tykání ('ty/jsi/máš'), even in onboarding, errors, or empty-state copy — this is professional pentest/security tooling used across teams and client engagements, not a consumer app.
styleNotes: Button and action labels use the infinitive verb form ('Uložit', 'Zrušit', 'Archivovat'), never a bare noun. Status/state badges use the neuter short passive-participle form ending in '-o' ('Dokončeno', 'Prolomeno', 'Zrušeno') regardless of the referent's grammatical gender, so status chips read consistently across the UI. Keep hashcat- and product-specific technical terms in English when there is no established Czech equivalent or a literal calque would mislead (hash, potfile, keyspace, loopback, benchmark, webhook, voucher) — decline them with Czech endings where natural ('hashe', 'hashů') rather than inventing awkward neologisms. Always keep full Czech diacritics (ě š č ř ž ý á í é ů ú ď ť ň); never strip them to save space in buttons or labels.

hash.note: Used as-is in professional Czech security usage, declined with Czech endings (hash, hashe, hashů); 'heš' is a marginal native spelling, not standard in professional contexts.

hashlist.note: Product-specific feature/page name (matches 'HashList' in the codebase); no established Czech equivalent.

hash type.note: The hashcat mode designation, e.g. NTLM (mode 1000).

crack.note: Verb: recover the plaintext of a hash; 'zlomit' is an alternative but less precise in a cryptography context.

cracked.note: Standalone status label/badge — use the neutral '-o' form, consistent with other status chips ('Dokončeno', 'Odesláno'). When modifying 'hash' directly in running text, use the agreeing adjective 'prolomený' (e.g. 'prolomený hash').

cracked hashes.note: These are hashes with a recovered plaintext, not passwords themselves — keep 'hash' and 'heslo'/'plaintext' distinct, they are separate glossary concepts in this product.

plaintext.note: Matches hashcat's own output terminology (hash:plaintext pairs); 'nešifrovaný text' reads as a generic cryptography term, not the specific recovered value shown in the UI.

potfile.note: hashcat-specific file format name; never translate a literal filename.

client potfile.note: 'Potfile' stays untranslated as in the base term; only the 'client' qualifier is localized.

wordlist.note: Standard in Czech security usage (cf. 'slovníkový útok' = dictionary attack).

rule.note: hashcat rule (password mangling rule); 'pravidlo' is the standard term.

attack mode.note: The category label for the attack-mode selector.

brute force.note: Matches the parallel structure of the other attack-mode entries (all end in 'útok'); bare 'Hrubá síla' would stand out inconsistently in the same dropdown as 'Slovníkový útok' / 'Hybridní útok'. This is also the standard Czech security term for the mode.

dictionary attack.note: The established Czech security term; 'útok ze slovníku' is a stiffer, less idiomatic literal rendering.

association attack.note: hashcat association attack (mode 9); a rarely-used, niche mode with no established Czech term, but the calque is understandable and matches the other attack-mode entries' adjective+'útok' pattern.

keyspace.note: hashcat's own term for the space of candidate passwords. A literal calque ('prostor klíčů') wrongly suggests cryptographic keys, which are not involved here — kept in English like 'hash'/'potfile' to avoid misleading professionals who read hashcat's own English output.

effective keyspace.note: Mixed form like 'Klientský potfile' — Czech qualifier plus the retained English base term 'keyspace', for the same reason as 'keyspace'.

chunk.note: One slice of a job's keyspace given to one agent; use 'blok', not 'kus'.

task.note: One chunk assignment running on an agent.

job.note: A cracking job against a hashlist; distinct from 'Úkol' (task) — keep the two visibly different in the UI.

workflow.note: An ordered sequence of preset jobs.

loopback.note: hashcat/product-specific feature name (re-run an attack using newly cracked passwords); 'zpětná smyčka' reads as an electronics/audio feedback-loop term and is not an established rendering here — kept as the feature's own name, like 'benchmark' or 'potfile'.

overflow.note: Extra agents given to a job beyond its limit; 'přetečení' is the standard Czech IT term for 'overflow' (cf. integer/capacity overflow) — 'přetok' is a plumbing/hydraulics term, not the usual computing sense.

benchmark.note: Speed test; 'benchmark' is standard as-is in Czech security tooling.

hash rate.note: Speed in hashes per second; matches common Czech usage in hashing/mining contexts.

progress.note: How much of the keyspace is done.

agent.note: Identical spelling in Czech; no translation needed.

claim code.note: Per terms.json this is the same concept as 'voucher' — use one consistent term across both the admin and agent-registration flows so users don't read them as two different things. 'Aktivační kód' is accurate but breaks that consistency.

voucher.note: Registration voucher; 'voucher' is a fully naturalized loanword in Czech (gift/discount vouchers) and is used as-is. Same underlying concept as 'claim code' — keep both rendered identically.

heartbeat.note: Periodic agent check-in; 'srdeční tep' is a literal translation but reads informally/biologically, not as a technical status signal.

offline buffer.note: Grace period before an agent is reported offline; 'ochranná lhůta' is the standard Czech legal/technical rendering of 'grace period' (cf. domain-registration grace periods). 'Časová rezerva odpojení' is unclear and non-standard.

binary.note: A hashcat binary version managed by the server.

client.note: Customer/engagement the hashlists belong to; 'zákazník' is more purely commercial, 'klient' matches pentest/consulting usage.

team.note: A group of users that share clients, hashlists and agents.

owner.note: The user an agent or resource belongs to.

retention.note: How long data is kept before deletion; 'uchovávání' (imperfective) matches the standard Czech GDPR/data-protection phrase 'doba uchovávání' (data retention period). 'Uchování' (perfective) is a workable alternative but less idiomatic for an ongoing policy.

archive.note: Button action (hide from default lists without deleting) — use the infinitive verb, the same pattern as 'apply' → 'Použít', not the noun 'Archiv'.

password reuse.note: Same password used by several accounts.

hash reuse.note: Same hash appearing for several accounts; parallel construction to 'password reuse'.

audit log.note: 'Log' is a fully naturalized loanword in Czech IT (cf. 'bezpečnostní log', 'log událostí'), but 'audit' should still take the Czech adjective form 'auditní' — leaving the whole phrase as unmarked English 'Audit log' reads as un-localized. 'Auditní protokol' is correct but noticeably more formal/verbose for UI.

autosave.note: Saved automatically when leaving a field.

apply.note: Button: put pending changes into effect; 'aplikovat' is an alternative but less native for a button label.

SAN.note: Subject Alternative Name; acronym kept as-is, as with other protocol/standard acronyms in doNotTranslate.

network share.note: SMB/NFS share used for wordlist storage.

mount.note: Attach a network share to a path; standard Czech IT verb for mounting.

cloud fleet.note: Rented cloud GPU instances. 'Cloud' is inflected as the Czech adjective 'cloudová' (cf. 'cloudové služby'); leaving the bare English noun 'Cloud' next to a Czech noun ('Cloud flotila') reads as a grammar error.

provisioning.note: Starting cloud instances automatically; matches standard Czech cloud documentation ('zřízení instance/prostředků'). 'Přidělování' is a workable alternative.

threshold.note: Percentage of budget that triggers an action; standard in Czech monitoring/alerting contexts ('prahová hodnota').

drain.note: Let running work finish without starting new work; matches the standard Czech rendering of 'drain' in cluster/orchestration contexts (cf. 'vyprázdnit uzel' for 'drain a node').

teardown.note: Destroying a cloud instance. Uses the same ongoing-process word-formation pattern as 'zřizování' (provisioning) and 'vyprazdňování' (drain) for a consistent lifecycle trio. 'Demontáž' evokes physically disassembling hardware, not terminating a cloud instance; 'rozpad' is a disintegration/breakup metaphor and equally off-target.

webhook.note: HTTP callback for notifications; universally kept as-is in Czech developer usage.

two-factor authentication.note: MFA; the standard Czech security term, matching 'two-factor' precisely.

authenticator app.note: TOTP app, e.g. Google Authenticator; standard Czech rendering.

API key.note: Personal key for the HTTP API; 'API' kept per doNotTranslate, 'klíč' translated.

branding.note: Custom app name, colours and logo; Czech business/software usage keeps the English term as-is.
